title: Nested binary64 all-reduction reconnaissance
objective: Add an explain-only structural compiler domain for checked nested binary64 all reductions, with stable proof and target rejection codes for scalar and fixed-pair finiteness predicates; do not implement an executable lowering.

oracles: structural AST fixtures and exact IR validation

handoff.summary: Added an application-name-independent, explain-only nested binary64 all-reduction recognizer, independently verified generic-fallback decision IR, and exact production/held-out/adversarial tests for scalar and fixed-pair finiteness predicates. The plugin owns no lowering and emits stable proof and target rejection codes.
risks: The plugin is intentionally not integrated into the shared catalog, optimizer index, or reason registry in this implementation lane.
Every semantic identity, representation, iteration, short-circuit, interrupt, and untouched-restart obligation remains an explicit rejection; no executable optimization is claimed.
The scratch worktree lacks the optional FLINT native addon, so four otherwise unrelated compiler fixtures fail module loading; the other 11 active compiler fixtures pass.
next_steps: Add the handed-off plugin to the integration-owned catalog at priority 145, export its domain from the optimizer index, and add the exact sorted reason-registry objects.
Regenerate the optimizer dashboard after integration changes the compiler identity.
Confirm both production grid-sampling regions appear as rejected observations through the integrated O2 compiler before developing any guarded representation proof or lowering.
